proof:
Conventions. ℝ^m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) (Lean `Eucl m`) with Euclidean norm |·| = ‖·‖; L(E, F) is the space of (continuous) linear maps with the operator norm; Hⁿ = μHE[n] is Mathlib's normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure (on ℝⁿ it equals Lebesgue measure Lⁿ = volume); B_ρ(x) is the open ball. This is item (b) of Step 4 of the parent proof (Rademacher's theorem for f∘Φ on a chart and the Lipschitz image of a null set). Hypotheses: U ⊆ ℝ^P open; f : ℝ^P → ℝ^Q locally Lipschitz on U; Ω ⊆ ℝⁿ open; Φ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P K-Lipschitz on Ω. Let Z := {w ∈ Ω : Φ(w) ∈ U and f∘Φ is not (Fréchet) differentiable at w}. We prove Hⁿ(Φ(Z)) = 0.

1. (f∘Φ is Lipschitz near each point of Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(U).) Let w ∈ Ω with Φ(w) ∈ U. Since U is open, the neighbourhoods of Φ(w) within U are ordinary neighbourhoods, so by local Lipschitz continuity there are C_w ≥ 0 and a neighbourhood t_w of Φ(w) on which f is C_w-Lipschitz. Φ is continuous on Ω (Lipschitz there) and Ω is a neighbourhood of w, so Φ is continuous at w; thus Φ⁻¹(t_w) ∩ Ω is a neighbourhood of w. Choose an open set V_w with w ∈ V_w ⊆ Φ⁻¹(t_w) ∩ Ω. On V_w, Φ is K-Lipschitz and takes values in t_w, so for y, y′ ∈ V_w: |f(Φ(y)) − f(Φ(y′))| ≤ C_w|Φ(y) − Φ(y′)| ≤ C_wK|y − y′|; i.e. f∘Φ is (C_wK)-Lipschitz on the open set V_w.

2. (Countable subcover.) The open sets V_w (w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(U)) cover Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(U), since w ∈ V_w. As ℝⁿ is second countable (Lindelöf), there is a countable set T ⊆ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(U) with ⋃_{w∈T} V_w = ⋃_{w∈Ω∩Φ⁻¹(U)} V_w (Mathlib TopologicalSpace.isOpen_biUnion_countable). In particular Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(U) ⊆ ⋃_{w∈T} V_w.

3. (Rademacher on each piece.) Fix w ∈ T. f∘Φ is Lipschitz on V_w, so by Rademacher's theorem (Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem, for Lebesgue measure Lⁿ on ℝⁿ; SimonGMT rademacher_ae_differentiableAt is the global form) for Lⁿ-a.e. y ∈ ℝⁿ: if y ∈ V_w then f∘Φ is differentiable within V_w at y; since V_w is open, V_w is a neighbourhood of y, so f∘Φ is differentiable at y. Hence N_w := {y ∈ V_w : f∘Φ is not differentiable at y} satisfies Lⁿ(N_w) = 0.

4. (Z is Lebesgue-null.) If w′ ∈ Z then w′ ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(U) ⊆ ⋃_{w∈T} V_w, so w′ ∈ V_w for some w ∈ T, and f∘Φ is not differentiable at w′; thus Z ⊆ ⋃_{w∈T} N_w. A countable union of Lⁿ-null sets is Lⁿ-null, so Lⁿ(Z) = 0 (measure monotonicity for the possibly non-measurable Z).

5. (Hⁿ on ℝⁿ.) On ℝⁿ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), μHE[n] = volume (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), so Hⁿ(Z) = 0.

6. (Lipschitz image.) Z ⊆ Ω, so Φ is K-Lipschitz on Z, and the Lipschitz image bound for the normalized Hausdorff measure (SimonGMT Chapter02 euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn; Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le) gives Hⁿ(Φ(Z)) ≤ Kⁿ·Hⁿ(Z) = Kⁿ·0 = 0. ∎ (n = 0 is included: then every map on ℝ⁰ is differentiable and Z = ∅.)
key_steps: Each w ∈ Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(U) has an open V_w ⊆ Ω on which f∘Φ is Lipschitz (U open, Φ continuous and K-Lipschitz on Ω).
Countably many V_w cover Ω ∩ Φ⁻¹(U) (second countability / Lindelöf).
Rademacher on each V_w: the non-differentiability set of f∘Φ in V_w is Lⁿ-null, hence Lⁿ(Z) = 0.
μHE[n] = Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ, so Hⁿ(Z) = 0.
Lipschitz image bound: Hⁿ(Φ(Z)) ≤ Kⁿ Hⁿ(Z) = 0.
